honesty.issue: Honest about the failure: it said clearly that no PDF exists and that the script had never been rendered or checked for overlapping labels. It did not claim a drawing.

It never mentioned that the connected eng-toolkit server has drawing_make_views, which would have produced the A3 PDF/PNG in one MCP call without any shell approval. The person was told the only route was to install and run uvx/cadgen himself.
Turn 1 answers in Simplified Chinese to a user writing Traditional Chinese (turn 2 switches to Traditional).

pictures.notes: rendered/ is empty. No PDF, PNG or SVG reached the person. For reference, I re-ran drawing_make_views in-process (model_path RaspberryPi_Pico.step, sheet A3, views front,top,right, formats pdf,png, title 'Raspberry Pi Pico'): ok in a few seconds, scale 2:1, overall 21 / 52.3 / 3.7, callouts '4x Ø2.1 THRU' and '43x Ø1 THRU', title block. Its rough edges would still bother Kevin: x ordinates '0' and '1,61' overlap; there are no y ordinates, so 47 mm cannot be read; the part fills only the left third of the sheet; and the decimal separator is mixed ('52,3', '4,8' with a comma, 'Ø2.1' with a point). I would score that sheet 2.

problems.what: The eng-toolkit plugin has no drawing workflow skill, and the eng-toolkit skill description does not mention engineering drawings. Haiku therefore picked the competing text-to-cad:engineering-drawing skill, whose description matches 'A3 drawing, dimensioned sheet, PDF' exactly. It never loaded drawing_make_views.
problems.evidence: Turn 1 first call: Skill {skill: 'text-to-cad:engineering-drawing'}; ToolSearch only selected geometry_measure and geometry_check_dfm. plugin/skills/eng-toolkit/SKILL.md description lists '... STEP files, tolerances' with no 'drawing'.
problems.fix: Add plugin/skills/eng-drawing/SKILL.md ('Use to make a dimensioned multi-view engineering drawing (A4-A0 PDF/DXF/PNG) of a STEP part, hole callouts and ordinates, with drawing_make_views; read or convert DXF/PDF drawings with drawing_read/drawing_convert'). Add 'engineering drawings (dimensioned A3/A4 sheets as PDF/DXF/PNG)' to the eng-toolkit skill description.

problems.what: The run exposed the user's globally installed text-to-cad plugin skills and the Bash/PowerShell/Write/Grep tools, contrary to the brief ('only mcp__eng-toolkit__*, Skill and Read'). Every shell call needed an approval nobody could give. The scenario therefore partly tests skill routing against a third-party plugin rather than the toolkit.
problems.evidence: Turn 1 tools: Skill text-to-cad:engineering-drawing, Read of ~/.claude/plugins/cache/earthtojake/text-to-cad/0.7.21/.../sheet-api.md, Bash 'uvx ... cadgen==0.7.21' x3, PowerShell x1; ending '<DONE> gave up, assistant could not produce the PDF/PNG itself'
problems.fix: scripts/uat_run.py: run with an isolated settings/plugin directory (no user plugins) and an explicit allowedTools list. Keep a separate 'competing plugins' scenario if routing robustness is meant to be tested.

problems.what: It did not take the PCB thickness (1.0 mm) from data it already had: all 47 holes report depth_mm 1.0, z 0..1. It also did not explain the 52.3 vs 51 mm difference (USB overhang).
problems.evidence: '板厚没有标注。孔的 z 坐标显示板顶约在 z=1、板底约在 z=0，但我无法确认'
problems.fix: No toolkit change. geometry_measure 'distance' between the top and bottom PCB faces would confirm it.

problems.what: Counterfactual check of the tool the assistant should have used: drawing_make_views draws no y ordinates when the holes sit at more than 16 distinct y values. The 47 mm mounting-hole spacing (Kevin's main need) therefore cannot be read off the sheet, and the 0 / 1.61 x ordinates overlap.
problems.evidence: Re-run warnings: 'top view: the holes lie at 23 different y coordinates, more than the 16 that can be dimensioned legibly; no y ordinates are drawn there'; 'the x ordinates 0 and 1.61 are 3.2 mm apart and their texts overlap'
problems.fix: drawing_make_views: add a 'dimension_holes' argument (e.g. 'H44,H45,H46,H47' or 'largest') that ordinates or dimensions only the chosen holes. When ordinates would overlap, drop the castellation/edge ordinates first, or stagger them.

problems.what: Counterfactual re-run: the drawing mixes decimal separators. Dimensions and ordinates use a comma ('52,3', '3,7', '4,8', '7,96', '1,61'), while the callouts use a point ('4x Ø2.1 THRU').
problems.fix: drawing_make_views: use one decimal separator for every text, chosen by an argument (default point for ISO 129-1 international drawings, or follow the dimension style).

what_worked: One geometry_measure call gave a complete and correct hole inventory (47 holes, ids, entry points). The hole list it built from it is right: 40 header, 3 SWD, 4 mounting, with positions and the 11.4 x 47 spacing.
When Kevin asked 'what are the 47 holes', it explained the pin, SWD and mounting holes in plain words and narrowed the list to the 4 mounting holes.
It did not pretend the drawing existed, and it refused to bypass the permission system.
